passage: Ecologist Ana Ferreira studied the marsh lantern, a small flowering plant that grows in dry grasslands. In her laboratory, marsh lantern seeds that were exposed to chemicals found in smoke sprouted within two weeks, while seeds kept away from smoke stayed dormant for the entire year of the study. Ferreira's findings suggest that in the wild, marsh lantern seeds are most likely to sprout ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: soon after a fire has burned through the grassland.
option_b: in years when no fire reaches the grassland at all.
option_c: only after spending more than a year in the soil.
option_d: more quickly in shaded forests than in open grasslands.
explanation_en:
Seeds sprouted quickly only after contact with smoke chemicals; without smoke they stayed dormant. In the wild, smoke comes from fires, so choice A is the logical prediction.

Choice B reverses the finding: without smoke the seeds did not sprout. Choice C is unsupported; smoke-exposed seeds sprouted within two weeks. Choice D brings in forests, which the study never examined.
explanation_uz:
Urug‘lar faqat tutun kimyoviy moddalari ta’siridan keyin tez unib chiqqan, tutunsiz esa tinim holatida qolgan. Tabiatda tutun yong‘indan paydo bo‘ladi, shuning uchun mantiqiy bashorat — A.

B natijani teskari aylantiradi: tutunsiz urug‘lar unmagan. C asossiz: tutun ta’sir qilgan urug‘lar ikki hafta ichida unib chiqqan. D o‘rmonlarni tilga oladi, tadqiqotda esa o‘rmonlar o‘rganilmagan.

passage: An undated letter by Gulnora Saidova, a schoolteacher in the town of Kemir, describes her first ride on the train from Kemir's new railway station, which she says "opened only last month." Town records show that the Kemir station opened in March 1889 and that no other station has ever served the town. This evidence suggests that Saidova's letter was most likely written ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: before the railway reached Kemir.
option_b: in or around April 1889.
option_c: many years after the station opened.
option_d: by someone other than Saidova.
explanation_en:
Saidova says the station opened "only last month," and the records date the opening to March 1889. The letter was therefore most likely written about a month later, in or around April 1889, as choice B says.

Choice A is impossible, since she describes riding the train from the station. Choice C conflicts with "only last month." Choice D has no support; nothing questions who wrote the letter.
explanation_uz:
Saidova bekat "faqat o‘tgan oy ochilgan" deb yozadi, hujjatlarga ko‘ra esa bekat 1889-yil martida ochilgan. Demak, maktub taxminan bir oydan keyin, ya’ni 1889-yil aprel atrofida yozilgan bo‘lishi ehtimoli katta — B.

A bo‘lishi mumkin emas, chunki u bekatdan poyezdda yurganini tasvirlaydi. C "faqat o‘tgan oy" degan so‘zlarga zid. D asossiz: maktub muallifi haqida hech qanday shubha bildirilmagan.

passage: The Darband City Museum began offering free admission every Monday. Over the following year, Monday attendance tripled, but attendance on the other six days of the week fell, and the museum's total weekly attendance stayed almost exactly the same as in the previous year. These figures suggest that the free-admission policy ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: attracted many people who had never visited the museum before.
option_b: caused the museum's income from ticket sales to rise sharply.
option_c: mostly led people who would have visited anyway to come on Mondays instead of on other days.
option_d: made Monday the least popular day to visit the museum.
explanation_en:
Monday attendance rose while the other days fell and the weekly total did not change. That pattern means visitors moved to Monday rather than new visitors arriving, as choice C says.

Choice A conflicts with the unchanged total. Choice B is unsupported and unlikely: the same number of people came, but more of them got in free. Choice D contradicts the tripling of Monday attendance.
explanation_uz:
Dushanbadagi tashriflar ko‘paygan, boshqa kunlardagisi kamaygan, haftalik jami esa o‘zgarmagan. Bu yangi tashrifchilar kelganini emas, balki odamlar tashrifni dushanbaga ko‘chirganini bildiradi — C.

A o‘zgarmagan jami songa zid. B asossiz va ehtimoldan yiroq: odamlar soni o‘sha-o‘sha, lekin ularning ko‘prog‘i bepul kirgan. D dushanbadagi tashriflar uch baravar oshganiga zid.

passage: The following text is from an original short story. Every evening Dilshod's grandmother set two cups on the low table, though she drank her tea alone. She always filled the second cup first, left it steaming beside her untouched, and poured it back into the pot only when the light had gone from the window. When Dilshod finally asked whom the cup was for, she smiled at the empty cushion across from her and said only that some habits outlive the people who began them. From her answer, Dilshod understood that the second cup ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: was being saved for him to drink after his lessons.
option_b: kept the tea warm until she was ready to drink it.
option_c: was a custom she had recently learned from a neighbor.
option_d: was a way of remembering someone who used to drink tea with her.
explanation_en:
She looks at an empty cushion and says that some habits "outlive the people who began them," which implies the person who shared tea with her is gone. The cup is a way of remembering that person, as choice D says.

Choice A is unsupported; the cup is poured back, not given to Dilshod. Choice B ignores her answer, and she never drinks from it. Choice C conflicts with the idea of an old habit that has outlived someone.
explanation_uz:
U bo‘sh ko‘rpachaga qarab, ba’zi odatlar "ularni boshlagan odamlardan uzoq yashaydi" deydi. Bu u bilan choy ichgan odam endi yo‘qligini anglatadi. Ikkinchi piyola o‘sha odamni xotirlash usuli — D.

A asossiz: piyoladagi choy Dilshodga berilmaydi, choynakka qaytariladi. B buvining javobini e’tiborsiz qoldiradi, u bu piyoladan hech ichmaydi. C kimdir vafotidan keyin ham davom etayotgan eski odat haqidagi fikrga zid.

passage: Entomologist Mei Lin Zhao found that the larvae of the copper-striped beetle feed only on the leaves of the silver willow. She surveyed twelve islands in a river delta and found the beetle on every island where silver willows grew and on none of the islands that lacked them. If a new island formed in the delta and silver willows never took root there, it would be reasonable to expect that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: the copper-striped beetle would not establish a lasting population on the island.
option_b: the beetle's larvae would begin feeding on other kinds of trees.
option_c: the island would soon have more beetles than any other island in the delta.
option_d: the island's soil would be unable to support any kind of tree.
explanation_en:
The larvae eat only silver willow leaves, and the beetle was absent from every island without the tree. An island with no silver willows would therefore not support a lasting beetle population, as choice A says.

Choice B contradicts the finding that the larvae feed only on silver willows. Choice C reverses the pattern. Choice D is unsupported; the text says nothing about other trees or the soil.
explanation_uz:
Qurt lichinkalari faqat kumush tol barglari bilan oziqlanadi, bu daraxt yo‘q orollarning birortasida qo‘ng‘iz topilmagan. Demak, kumush tol o‘smagan orolda qo‘ng‘iz doimiy yashay olmaydi — A.

B lichinkalar faqat kumush tol bilan oziqlanishiga zid. C qonuniyatni teskari aylantiradi. D asossiz: matnda boshqa daraxtlar yoki tuproq haqida gap yo‘q.

passage: Account books from the port town of Selvik show that the price of bread there usually changed very little from year to year. During one unusually cold winter, however, the harbor stayed frozen from December to May, no ships could reach the town, and the price of bread more than doubled. Once the ice melted and ships returned, the price quickly fell back to its usual level. These records suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: Selvik's bakers raised their prices every winter.
option_b: Selvik relied heavily on grain or flour brought in by ship.
option_c: farmers near Selvik grew more grain during cold winters.
option_d: bread cost more in Selvik than in any other town in the region.
explanation_en:
Bread prices jumped only when ships could not arrive and dropped as soon as ships returned. This link suggests the town depended on shipped grain or flour, as choice B says.

Choice A contradicts the statement that prices usually changed very little. Choice C is unsupported, and more local grain would not explain a price rise. Choice D makes a comparison with other towns that the text never mentions.
explanation_uz:
Non narxi faqat kemalar kela olmagan paytda keskin oshgan va kemalar qaytishi bilan pasaygan. Bu bog‘liqlik shaharning kemada keltiriladigan don yoki unga tayanganini ko‘rsatadi — B.

A narx odatda deyarli o‘zgarmagani haqidagi gapga zid. C asossiz, qolaversa, mahalliy don ko‘paysa, narx oshmasdi. D matnda umuman tilga olinmagan boshqa shaharlar bilan solishtiradi.

passage: The flowers of the moonbell vine, a climbing plant, stay tightly closed during the day and open only after sunset, when they release a strong sweet scent. Botanist Kamila Usmonova found that the plant's pollen is carried from flower to flower only by animals that visit the open flowers. Because the flowers are open only at night, Usmonova concluded that the moonbell vine is most likely pollinated by ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: bees that feed during the hottest hours of the day.
option_b: wind that blows across the closed flowers.
option_c: animals that are active after dark, such as certain moths.
option_d: birds that visit the flowers in the early morning.
explanation_en:
Pollen is moved only by animals that visit open flowers, and the flowers are open only at night. The pollinators must therefore be animals active after dark, as choice C says.

Choices A and D name daytime visitors, but the flowers are closed in the daytime. Choice B contradicts the finding that only animals carry the pollen.
explanation_uz:
Changni faqat ochiq gullarga qo‘nadigan hayvonlar tashiydi, gullar esa faqat kechasi ochiladi. Demak, changlatuvchilar qorong‘ida faol bo‘ladigan hayvonlar bo‘lishi kerak — C.

A va D kunduzi uchadigan hayvonlarni ko‘rsatadi, lekin kunduzi gullar yopiq. B changni faqat hayvonlar tashiydi degan xulosaga zid.

passage: Before 2024, the train station in the town of Kelvar had no place to lock bicycles, and nearly all commuters drove to the station and parked in its crowded lot. After the town installed 200 bicycle racks, the number of bicycles at the station rose from a handful to more than 150 on a typical weekday, and for the first time the parking lot had empty spaces every morning. The total number of people taking the train stayed about the same. This suggests that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: fewer people commuted by train after the racks were installed.
option_b: the station's parking lot was made larger at the same time.
option_c: commuters who cycle live farther from the station than commuters who drive.
option_d: some commuters who had been driving to the station began cycling there instead.
explanation_en:
Train ridership stayed the same, yet bicycles appeared and parking spaces opened up. The simplest explanation is that some drivers switched to cycling, as choice D says.

Choice A contradicts the steady number of train riders. Choice B is unsupported; the text mentions only the new racks. Choice C makes a claim about distance that the text never addresses.
explanation_uz:
Poyezd yo‘lovchilari soni o‘zgarmagan, lekin velosipedlar paydo bo‘lgan va avtoturargohda bo‘sh joylar ochilgan. Eng oddiy izoh — mashinada kelganlarning bir qismi velosipedga o‘tgan — D.

A yo‘lovchilar soni o‘zgarmagani haqidagi gapga zid. B asossiz: matnda faqat yangi velosiped tirgaklari tilga olinadi. C masofa haqida da’vo qiladi, matnda bu haqda gap yo‘q.

passage: At a medieval site near the village of Qorasuv, archaeologists uncovered a long building containing six large clay ovens, dozens of stone tools for grinding grain, and layers of charred wheat on the floor. They found no beds, no small hearths for heating, and none of the household objects, such as cooking pots and storage jars for personal use, that are common in homes from the same period. The archaeologists concluded that the building was most likely used as ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: a place where bread was produced in large quantities.
option_b: a family home for several generations.
option_c: a storehouse where grain was kept but never processed.
option_d: a workshop where clay pots were made and fired.
explanation_en:
Large ovens, grinding tools and burned wheat all point to turning grain into bread, and the many ovens suggest large-scale work. Choice A fits all the evidence.

Choice B conflicts with the missing beds and household objects. Choice C ignores the grinding tools and ovens, which show the grain was processed. Choice D could explain ovens, but not the grinding tools or the wheat, and no pots were found.
explanation_uz:
Katta tandirlar, don maydalaydigan toshlar va kuygan bug‘doy — bularning barchasi donni nonga aylantirishni ko‘rsatadi, tandirlarning ko‘pligi esa ishning katta hajmda bo‘lganini bildiradi. Barcha dalillarga A mos keladi.

B to‘shaklar va uy-ro‘zg‘or buyumlari yo‘qligiga zid. C maydalash asboblari va tandirlarni e’tiborsiz qoldiradi, ular don qayta ishlanganini ko‘rsatadi. D tandirlarni izohlashi mumkin, lekin maydalash toshlari va bug‘doyni izohlamaydi, qolaversa, sopol idishlar topilmagan.

passage: Hydrologist Timur Nazarov measured the water level in a village well every week for three years. Each year, the level fell steadily from June through August, the months when nearby farms pump groundwater to water their crops, and rose again after the pumping stopped in September. Rainfall in the area, by contrast, was spread fairly evenly across the year. Nazarov's data suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: heavy summer rains are the main cause of the drop in the well's water level.
option_b: the farms' pumping is likely drawing down the same groundwater that supplies the well.
option_c: the well will run completely dry within the next three years.
option_d: the farms pump more water in September than in any other month.
explanation_en:
The well's level fell exactly while the farms pumped and recovered when they stopped, while rainfall stayed steady. The pumping is therefore the likely cause, which means it draws on the same groundwater, as choice B says.

Choice A conflicts with the even rainfall, and rain would raise, not lower, the level. Choice C goes too far; the level recovered each year. Choice D contradicts the statement that pumping stopped in September.
explanation_uz:
Quduqdagi suv sathi aynan fermalar suv tortgan oylarda pasaygan va to‘xtatilgach tiklangan, yog‘ingarchilik esa yil bo‘yi bir tekis bo‘lgan. Demak, sabab suv tortish bo‘lishi ehtimoli katta va fermalar quduq bilan bir xil yer osti suvidan foydalanadi — B.

A bir tekis yog‘ingarchilikka zid, qolaversa, yomg‘ir sathni pasaytirmaydi, balki ko‘taradi. C haddan oshadi: sath har yili tiklangan. D suv tortish sentyabrda to‘xtagani haqidagi gapga zid.

passage: Membership lists of the scribes' guild in the city of Altinsoy show between 40 and 45 members every year from 1820 to 1850. In 1851 the city's first printing shop opened. Over the next decade, the guild's membership fell to 12, while the printing shop grew from three workers to thirty, and the city's demand for copied documents did not decline. A reasonable conclusion is that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: the guild had stopped admitting new members well before 1850.
option_b: most of the guild's former members moved to larger cities to find work.
option_c: much of the copying work once done by scribes shifted to the printing shop.
option_d: the printing shop hired only former members of the scribes' guild.
explanation_en:
Demand for copies stayed the same, but scribes declined just as the printing shop grew. The work most likely moved from scribes to the printing shop, as choice C says.

Choice A conflicts with the steady membership through 1850. Choice B is unsupported; the text says nothing about where former scribes went. Choice D is too extreme; nothing says who the shop hired.
explanation_uz:
Hujjat nusxalariga talab kamaymagan, lekin bosmaxona o‘sgan paytda kotiblar soni kamaygan. Demak, nusxa ko‘chirish ishi kotiblardan bosmaxonaga o‘tgan — C.

A 1850-yilgacha a’zolar soni barqaror bo‘lganiga zid. B asossiz: sobiq kotiblar qayerga ketgani aytilmagan. D haddan oshadi: bosmaxona kimni ishga olgani haqida hech narsa deyilmagan.

passage: Cracks often form in roads when water seeps into small openings near the surface, freezes, and expands. Engineer Lola Rashidova tested a porous pavement that lets water drain all the way through to a layer of gravel below instead of collecting near the surface. After two winters, test sections of the porous pavement showed far fewer cracks than sections of ordinary pavement on the same street. This result suggests that the porous pavement cracked less because ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: it was laid in a warmer part of the city than the ordinary pavement was.
option_b: drivers avoided using the test sections during the winter.
option_c: it held more water near its surface than ordinary pavement did.
option_d: less water stayed near its surface, where it could freeze and expand.
explanation_en:
The text explains that cracks come from water freezing near the surface, and the porous pavement drains that water away. So less water was there to freeze and expand, as choice D says.

Choice A is ruled out because both kinds of pavement were on the same street. Choice B has no support. Choice C reverses how the porous pavement works.
explanation_uz:
Matnda yoriqlar yuza yaqinida muzlagan suvdan paydo bo‘lishi tushuntiriladi, g‘ovak qoplama esa bu suvni pastga o‘tkazib yuboradi. Demak, muzlab kengayadigan suv kamroq qolgan — D.

A rad etiladi, chunki ikkala qoplama bir ko‘chada bo‘lgan. B asossiz. C g‘ovak qoplama qanday ishlashini teskari aylantiradi.

passage: Every autumn, flocks of amber warblers stop for several days at Lake Tuzkon during their southward migration. Ornithologist Aziz Qodirov considered two explanations: the birds stop to feed on the lake's insects, or they stop mainly to rest before crossing the large desert to the south. Qodirov found that as many warblers stopped at the lake in years when insects there were scarce as in years when insects were plentiful, and that the birds spent most of each day perched and inactive. These observations suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: the warblers would skip Lake Tuzkon entirely in years when insects there were scarce.
option_b: resting, rather than feeding, is more likely the main reason the warblers stop at the lake.
option_c: the warblers eat nothing at all while they stay at the lake.
option_d: the desert to the south has more insects than Lake Tuzkon does.
explanation_en:
If food were the main reason, fewer birds should stop when insects are scarce, but the number did not change, and the birds spent most of their time inactive. Both findings favor the rest explanation, as choice B says.

Choice A contradicts the finding that just as many birds stopped in poor insect years. Choice C is too extreme; resting most of the day does not mean never eating. Choice D compares the lake with the desert, which the text does not do.
explanation_uz:
Agar asosiy sabab ozuqa bo‘lganida, hasharotlar kam yillarda qushlar kamroq to‘xtashi kerak edi, lekin ularning soni o‘zgarmagan va qushlar vaqtining ko‘p qismini harakatsiz o‘tkazgan. Ikkala kuzatuv ham dam olish izohini qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi — B.

A hasharotlar kam yillarda ham shuncha qush to‘xtagani haqidagi natijaga zid. C haddan oshadi: kunning ko‘p qismida dam olish umuman ovqatlanmaslikni anglatmaydi. D ko‘lni cho‘l bilan solishtiradi, matnda bunday taqqoslash yo‘q.

passage: In 1862, the scholar Edmund Hale published an English translation of a Persian collection of fables, claiming that he had worked directly from the Persian original. Yet Hale's version contains seven mistakes, such as calling a jackal a fox, that have no basis in the Persian text but match mistakes in a French translation published in 1838. Moreover, three fables that the French translator left out are also missing from Hale's version. This evidence suggests that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: the French translator copied his mistakes from Hale's translation.
option_b: the Persian original contains many errors about animals.
option_c: Hale relied on the French translation rather than working only from the Persian original.
option_d: Hale could not read French and therefore misunderstood the fables.
explanation_en:
Hale's errors are not in the Persian text but match the earlier French translation, and he omits the same fables the French translator omitted. The likeliest explanation is that he used the French version, as choice C says.

Choice A reverses the timeline: the French translation appeared in 1838, before Hale's in 1862. Choice B contradicts the statement that the mistakes have no basis in the Persian text. Choice D is the opposite of what the shared errors suggest.
explanation_uz:
Hale xatolari fors matnida yo‘q, lekin avvalroq chiqqan fransuzcha tarjimadagi xatolarga mos keladi, u fransuz tarjimon tashlab ketgan o‘sha masallarni ham tushirib qoldirgan. Eng ehtimoliy izoh — u fransuzcha tarjimadan foydalangan — C.

A vaqt tartibini teskari qiladi: fransuzcha tarjima 1838-yilda, Hale tarjimasidan (1862) oldin chiqqan. B xatolarning fors matnida asosi yo‘qligiga zid. D umumiy xatolar ko‘rsatayotgan narsaning aksini aytadi.

passage: A school library began awarding students one point for each book they finished, with prizes for the students who earned the most points. During the program, the number of books borrowed rose by 60 percent, but the average length of a borrowed book fell from 210 pages to 140 pages, so the total number of pages borrowed rose only slightly. The library's collection did not change during this time. These results suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: students read far more pages in total during the program than they had before it.
option_b: the library added many short books to its collection just before the program began.
option_c: students lost interest in reading once the program began.
option_d: many students responded to the program by choosing shorter books so they could earn points faster.
explanation_en:
Points were given per book, not per page, and students began borrowing many more but much shorter books from an unchanged collection. That shift suggests students picked short books to collect points quickly, as choice D says.

Choice A contradicts the statement that total pages rose only slightly. Choice B is ruled out because the collection did not change. Choice C conflicts with the 60 percent rise in borrowing.
explanation_uz:
Ball sahifa uchun emas, kitob uchun berilgan va o‘quvchilar o‘zgarmagan fonddan ancha ko‘p, lekin ancha qisqa kitoblar ola boshlagan. Bu o‘quvchilar ballni tezroq to‘plash uchun qisqa kitoblarni tanlaganini ko‘rsatadi — D.

A jami sahifalar soni ozgina oshgani haqidagi gapga zid. B rad etiladi, chunki kutubxona fondi o‘zgarmagan. C kitob olish 60 foizga oshganiga zid.

passage: Pharmacologist Hana Sato found that a compound called K-17 lowered blood sugar in ordinary laboratory mice. She then gave K-17 to mice that had been bred to lack RX2, a protein found in the liver. In these mice, K-17 had no effect on blood sugar, although the same mice responded normally to other compounds known to lower blood sugar. These results suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: K-17 most likely lowers blood sugar through a process that depends on RX2.
option_b: mice that lack RX2 cannot have their blood sugar lowered by any compound.
option_c: RX2 raises blood sugar in mice that are not given K-17.
option_d: K-17 would lower blood sugar more effectively in humans than in mice.
explanation_en:
K-17 worked only in mice that had RX2, while mice without RX2 still responded to other compounds. So the failure was specific to K-17, which points to K-17 needing RX2, as choice A says.

Choice B contradicts the normal response to other compounds. Choice C is unsupported; the study shows nothing about what RX2 does on its own. Choice D brings in humans, who were not studied.
explanation_uz:
K-17 faqat RX2 oqsili bor sichqonlarda ta’sir qilgan, RX2 siz sichqonlar esa boshqa moddalarga odatdagidek javob bergan. Demak, muammo faqat K-17 ga xos va bu modda ta’sir qilishi uchun RX2 kerak — A.

B boshqa moddalarga normal javob berilganiga zid. C asossiz: tadqiqot RX2 ning o‘zi nima qilishini ko‘rsatmaydi. D odamlarni tilga oladi, ular o‘rganilmagan.

passage: The following text is from an original short story. Nargiza has just received a letter offering her a job in the capital. She read the letter twice at the kitchen table and then folded it into a small, careful square. All afternoon she worked in the orchard beside her father without mentioning the offer, though twice she stopped to look down the road that led to the station. That evening, when he asked why she was so quiet, she began to answer, glanced at the rows of apricot trees he had planted the year she was born, and ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: laughed and announced that she had already bought a train ticket.
option_b: said only that she was tired from the long day.
option_c: tore up the letter in front of him to show that she would never leave.
option_d: told him angrily that the orchard had kept her from living her own life.
explanation_en:
Nargiza keeps the offer to herself all day, starts to answer, then looks at the trees that tie her to her father, which shows hesitation. Avoiding the subject with a vague excuse, as in choice B, fits that hesitation.

Choice A conflicts with her secrecy and uncertain looks down the road. Choice C is too dramatic and certain; she has carefully kept the letter. Choice D adds anger that nothing in her quiet, careful behavior suggests.
explanation_uz:
Nargiza kun bo‘yi taklif haqida hech kimga aytmaydi, javob bermoqchi bo‘ladi-yu, uni otasiga bog‘lab turgan daraxtlarga ko‘z tashlaydi — bu ikkilanishni ko‘rsatadi. Mavzudan noaniq bahona bilan chetlab o‘tish, ya’ni B, shu ikkilanishga mos keladi.

A uning sir saqlashi va yo‘lga ikkilanib qarashiga zid. C haddan tashqari keskin va qat’iy: u maktubni ehtiyotkorlik bilan saqlab qo‘ygan. D g‘azabni qo‘shadi, uning sokin va ehtiyotkor xatti-harakatida bunga ishora yo‘q.

passage: A merchant's account book from the trading town of Yarkam, dated 1640, records payments to a painter for "the boot over the shoemaker's door" and "the golden key for the locksmith's." Town records from the same decade show that fewer than one in five adults in Yarkam could sign their own name. Historian Malika Yo'ldosheva argues that the town's shop signs were most likely pictures rather than written names, because ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: painters in Yarkam were unable to paint letters.
option_b: the town's laws prohibited written words on shop signs.
option_c: pictures would have identified shops for the many residents who could not read.
option_d: merchants wanted to hide what they sold from tax collectors.
explanation_en:
The account book describes picture signs (a boot, a key), and most adults could not even sign their names. A picture would let people who could not read find the right shop, which is the reasoning in choice C.

Choices A and B invent restrictions the text never mentions. Choice D contradicts the purpose of a sign that shows what the shop sells, such as a boot for a shoemaker.
explanation_uz:
Hisob daftarida rasmli peshlavhalar (etik, kalit) tilga olinadi, kattalarning aksariyati esa hatto o‘z ismini ham yoza olmagan. Rasm o‘qiy olmaydigan odamlarga kerakli do‘konni topishga yordam bergan — bu C dagi mulohaza.

A va B matnda tilga olinmagan cheklovlarni o‘ylab topadi. D do‘kon nima sotishini ko‘rsatadigan peshlavha (masalan, etikdo‘z uchun etik) maqsadiga zid.

passage: To estimate how common the spotted forest deer is in a national park, biologist Jamshid Hakimov placed motion-triggered cameras at forty locations during the dry season, every one of them beside a stream or pond. His cameras recorded deer far more often than the cameras in the park's previous survey, which had been placed at randomly chosen points. Before concluding that the deer population has grown, Hakimov should consider that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: the previous survey used cameras at more locations than his survey did.
option_b: deer avoid streams and ponds during the dry season.
option_c: the park's deer population may have declined since the previous survey.
option_d: deer may gather near water during the dry season, so cameras placed there could record them more often even if their numbers had not changed.
explanation_en:
Hakimov placed every camera at water during the dry season, while the earlier survey used random points. If deer cluster at water in dry weather, his cameras would see more deer without any population growth, as choice D says.

Choice A is unsupported and would not explain more sightings. Choice B, if true, would make his higher count harder to explain, not easier. Choice C simply asserts a decline with no evidence behind it.
explanation_uz:
Hakimov barcha kameralarni quruq mavsumda suv yoniga qo‘ygan, avvalgi tadqiqotda esa nuqtalar tasodifiy tanlangan. Agar bug‘ular qurg‘oqchilikda suv atrofida to‘plansa, uning kameralari bug‘ular soni o‘smasa ham ularni ko‘proq qayd etadi — D.

A asossiz va ko‘proq qayd etilganini izohlamaydi. B, agar to‘g‘ri bo‘lsa, uning yuqori natijasini izohlashni osonlashtirmaydi, aksincha qiyinlashtiradi. C hech qanday dalilsiz kamayish haqida da’vo qiladi.

passage: Folklorist Dilfuza Mamatova collected 30 versions of a traditional wedding song from villages across a wide valley. Every version shared the same melody and the same first four verses. A fifth verse, which names the Sharob River and praises its fishermen, appeared only in the eleven versions collected from villages on the river's banks. The oldest written copy of the song, made in 1790 in a village far from the river, contains only the first four verses. Mamatova reasoned that the fifth verse was most likely ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: added later by singers in the river villages to an older, shared song.
option_b: sung in every village in the valley before 1790.
option_c: the reason the melody differs in the river villages.
option_d: written by fishermen who came from outside the valley.
explanation_en:
All versions share four verses, the oldest copy has only those four, and the fifth verse, which is about the river, appears only near the river. That pattern suggests river-village singers added it to an older song, as choice A says.

Choice B conflicts with the 1790 copy and with the verse's absence elsewhere. Choice C contradicts the statement that every version has the same melody. Choice D is unsupported; nothing indicates outsiders wrote the verse.
explanation_uz:
Barcha variantlarda to‘rtta umumiy band bor, eng qadimgi nusxada ham faqat shu to‘rttasi bor, daryo haqidagi beshinchi band esa faqat daryo bo‘yidagi qishloqlarda uchraydi. Bu daryo bo‘yi qo‘shiqchilari uni eski qo‘shiqqa keyinroq qo‘shganini ko‘rsatadi — A.

B 1790-yilgi nusxaga va bandning boshqa joylarda yo‘qligiga zid. C barcha variantlarda kuy bir xil ekani haqidagi gapga zid. D asossiz: bandni tashqaridan kelganlar yozgani haqida hech qanday ishora yo‘q.

passage: Plant ecologist Sevinch Abdullayeva grew sorghum seedlings in soil collected from a farm field. She heated half of the soil to kill every living thing in it and left the rest untreated. Seedlings in the heated soil grew much more slowly than those in untreated soil. But when she mixed a single spoonful of untreated soil into a pot of heated soil, the seedlings grew as well as those in untreated soil. Since a spoonful of soil adds almost no nutrients to a pot, these results suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: heating the soil produced chemicals that are harmful to sorghum.
option_b: living organisms in the untreated soil help sorghum grow.
option_c: sorghum grows best in soil that contains no living organisms.
option_d: the farm's soil contains too few nutrients for sorghum to grow well.
explanation_en:
A tiny amount of untreated soil, adding almost no nutrients, fully restored growth. Living organisms can multiply from a small sample, so the likeliest explanation is that living things in the soil help sorghum, as choice B says.

Choice A is tempting, but a single spoonful could hardly cancel out harmful chemicals in a whole pot. Choice C reverses the result. Choice D conflicts with the normal growth in untreated soil.
explanation_uz:
Ozuqa deyarli qo‘shmaydigan bir qoshiq ishlov berilmagan tuproq o‘sishni to‘liq tiklagan. Tirik organizmlar kichik namunadan ko‘payishi mumkin, shuning uchun eng ehtimoliy izoh — tuproqdagi tirik organizmlar jo‘xori o‘sishiga yordam beradi — B.

A jozibali, lekin bir qoshiq tuproq butun tuvakdagi zararli moddalarni yo‘qota olmaydi. C natijani teskari aylantiradi. D ishlov berilmagan tuproqda o‘sish normal bo‘lganiga zid.

passage: In his published travel book, the explorer Konstantin Varga gives a vivid account of the spring horse fair in the city of Tashan, describing the colors of the banners and the order of the races. Varga's private diary, however, records that he spent the entire spring of that year in a town more than 400 kilometers from Tashan and did not arrive in Tashan until midsummer. The fair has always been held only in spring. Taken together, this evidence suggests that Varga's account of the fair ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: proves that the fair was held in midsummer in the year he visited.
option_b: was copied directly from the entries in his private diary.
option_c: was most likely based on information he obtained from others rather than on his own observation.
option_d: contains no accurate details about the fair.
explanation_en:
Varga's diary places him far away during the spring, and the fair happens only in spring, so he could not have seen it. His account most likely came from what others told him, as choice C says.

Choice A contradicts the statement that the fair is always held in spring. Choice B conflicts with the diary, which shows he was elsewhere. Choice D goes too far; secondhand information can still be accurate.
explanation_uz:
Varga kundaligiga ko‘ra u bahor bo‘yi uzoqda bo‘lgan, yarmarka esa faqat bahorda o‘tkaziladi, demak, u yarmarkani ko‘rmagan. Uning tasviri boshqalardan eshitgan ma’lumotlarga asoslangan bo‘lishi ehtimoli katta — C.

A yarmarka doim bahorda o‘tkazilishiga zid. B kundalikka zid, kundalik uning boshqa joyda bo‘lganini ko‘rsatadi. D haddan oshadi: boshqalardan olingan ma’lumot ham to‘g‘ri bo‘lishi mumkin.

passage: Urban planner Shahlo Nematova found that residents of neighborhoods with many street trees filed fewer complaints about summer heat than did residents of neighborhoods with few trees. She also found, however, that homes in the tree-lined neighborhoods were far more likely to have air conditioning than homes in the other neighborhoods. Therefore, Nematova's findings alone do not establish that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: residents of tree-lined neighborhoods filed fewer complaints about summer heat.
option_b: homes in tree-lined neighborhoods were more likely to have air conditioning.
option_c: the number of heat complaints differed between the two kinds of neighborhoods.
option_d: street trees are the reason that residents of tree-lined neighborhoods complained less about heat.
explanation_en:
Air conditioning, not trees, could explain the fewer complaints, so the findings do not show that trees caused the difference, as choice D says.

Choices A, B and C are all things Nematova directly observed, so her findings do establish them. The missing step is only the causal claim about trees.
explanation_uz:
Shikoyatlar kamligini daraxtlar emas, konditsionerlar ham izohlashi mumkin, shuning uchun natijalar farqga daraxtlar sabab bo‘lganini isbotlamaydi — D.

A, B va C — Nematova bevosita kuzatgan narsalar, ya’ni ularni natijalar isbotlaydi. Isbotlanmagan narsa faqat daraxtlar sabab ekani haqidagi da’vo.

passage: Sediment cores from the bottom of Lake Ozod contain a thin layer of volcanic ash. Chemical tests match the ash to an eruption of Mount Karatog, which other evidence dates to about 1450. In the sediment below the ash, most of the preserved pollen comes from oak trees; in the sediment above it, most of the pollen comes from grasses, and oak pollen is rare. These findings suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: the land around the lake shifted from oak forest toward grassland at some point after about 1450.
option_b: the eruption of Mount Karatog killed every oak tree near the lake at once.
option_c: oak trees were more common around the lake after 1450 than before it.
option_d: the ash layer formed long before Mount Karatog erupted.
explanation_en:
Sediment builds up from the bottom, so layers below the ash are older than 1450 and layers above are younger. Oak pollen dominates before and grass pollen after, so the vegetation shifted toward grassland after about 1450, as choice A says.

Choice B claims a cause and a sudden, total change that the evidence does not show. Choice C reverses the pollen pattern. Choice D contradicts the chemical match between the ash and the eruption.
explanation_uz:
Cho‘kindilar pastdan yuqoriga qarab yig‘iladi, demak, kul ostidagi qatlamlar 1450-yildan qadimiyroq, ustidagilari esa yangiroq. Avval eman changi, keyin o‘t changi ko‘p bo‘lgan, ya’ni taxminan 1450-yildan keyin o‘simlik qoplami o‘tloqqa tomon o‘zgargan — A.

B dalillar ko‘rsatmagan sabab va to‘satdan, to‘liq o‘zgarishni da’vo qiladi. C chang qonuniyatini teskari aylantiradi. D kul bilan otilish o‘rtasidagi kimyoviy moslikka zid.

passage: Biologist Odina Rahmonova found that a colony of long-eared bats caught about twice as many moths on moonless nights as on moonlit nights. She considered two explanations: moths might be more active on dark nights, or the bats might spend more time hunting when the sky is dark. Light traps set near the colony caught about the same number of moths on moonlit and moonless nights, while tracking tags showed that the bats spent about twice as long outside their roost on moonless nights. Rahmonova's results suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: the bats avoid hunting on moonlit nights because owls catch bats more easily then.
option_b: moths are more active on moonlit nights than on moonless nights.
option_c: the bats' larger catch on moonless nights can be explained by the extra time they spent hunting rather than by a change in moth activity.
option_d: the bats catch moths at a much faster rate per hour on moonless nights.
explanation_en:
Moth numbers were the same on both kinds of night, but the bats hunted about twice as long and caught about twice as many. The extra hunting time alone accounts for the larger catch, as choice C says.

Choice A offers a reason (owls) that the study never tested, so it goes beyond the evidence. Choice B contradicts the equal light-trap counts. Choice D is a subtle trap: twice the catch in twice the time means the hourly rate stayed about the same.
explanation_uz:
Ikkala turdagi tunda ham kuya soni bir xil bo‘lgan, ammo ko‘rshapalaklar taxminan ikki baravar uzoq ov qilib, taxminan ikki baravar ko‘p kuya tutgan. Ov vaqtining uzayishi o‘zi katta o‘ljani izohlaydi — C.

A tadqiqotda tekshirilmagan sababni (boyo‘g‘lilar) keltiradi, ya’ni dalildan tashqariga chiqadi. B tuzoqlarda bir xil son qayd etilganiga zid. D nozik tuzoq: ikki baravar vaqtda ikki baravar o‘lja — soatbay tezlik deyarli o‘zgarmagan degani.

passage: Because the earliest surviving chronicle of the town of Brenholt first mentions the town's stone bridge in an entry for 1320, historians have usually dated the bridge's construction to that year. Historian Ruth Aldane notes, however, that a tax roll from 1305 lists income from a toll "at the Brenholt crossing," and that in this region, tolls of that kind were collected only at bridges, never at fords or ferries. She also points out that the chronicle's 1320 entry describes repairs made to the bridge after a flood. Aldane's evidence suggests that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: a bridge already stood at Brenholt before 1320, so the chronicle entry does not mark when the town's first bridge was built.
option_b: the stone bridge that the chronicle mentions was completed in 1305.
option_c: the chronicle's dates for events in Brenholt are generally unreliable.
option_d: Brenholt stopped collecting tolls at the crossing after the flood of 1320.
explanation_en:
A bridge toll in 1305 means some bridge existed then, and an entry about repairs implies the bridge was already standing in 1320. So 1320 is not the date the first bridge was built, as choice A says.

Choice B is too precise: the 1305 toll shows that a bridge existed, not that the stone bridge was finished that year (it could have been an earlier bridge). Choice C overgeneralizes; Aldane questions one inference, not all of the chronicle's dates. Choice D is unsupported.
explanation_uz:
1305-yilda ko‘prik boji olingani o‘sha paytda qandaydir ko‘prik bo‘lganini anglatadi, 1320-yilgi yozuv esa ta’mir haqida, ya’ni ko‘prik allaqachon mavjud bo‘lgan. Demak, 1320-yil birinchi ko‘prik qurilgan sana emas — A.

B haddan tashqari aniq: 1305-yilgi boj ko‘prik borligini ko‘rsatadi, lekin aynan tosh ko‘prik o‘sha yili qurib bitkazilganini ko‘rsatmaydi (u avvalgi boshqa ko‘prik bo‘lishi mumkin). C haddan ortiq umumlashtiradi: Aldane yilnomaning barcha sanalarini emas, bitta xulosani shubha ostiga oladi. D asossiz.

passage: The leaves of the steppe sage produce a bitter compound when caterpillars feed on them. To learn what triggers this response, botanist Zebo Haydarova cut some leaves with scissors, cut others with scissors and then brushed caterpillar saliva onto the cuts, and left a third group untouched. Leaves cut with scissors alone produced only slightly more of the compound than untouched leaves did, whereas leaves that received both cuts and saliva produced nearly as much as leaves that caterpillars had actually eaten. These results suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: the steppe sage produces large amounts of the compound in response to any kind of damage to its leaves.
option_b: caterpillar saliva brushed onto undamaged leaves would trigger as strong a response as caterpillar feeding does.
option_c: the bitter compound protects the steppe sage from being eaten by caterpillars.
option_d: something in caterpillar saliva, together with wounding, is largely responsible for the plant's strong response to feeding.
explanation_en:
Cutting alone barely raised the compound, but cutting plus saliva nearly matched real feeding. So the strong response depends on the saliva combined with the wounds, as choice D says.

Choice A contradicts the weak response to scissor cuts. Choice B goes beyond the experiment: saliva was tested only on cut leaves, never on undamaged ones. Choice C may sound reasonable, but the study measured what triggers the compound, not whether it deters caterpillars.
explanation_uz:
Faqat qaychi bilan kesish moddani deyarli ko‘paytirmagan, kesish va so‘lak birgalikda esa haqiqiy yeyilishga deyarli teng natija bergan. Demak, kuchli javob so‘lak va jarohat birgalikda bo‘lishiga bog‘liq — D.

A qaychi bilan kesishga kuchsiz javob berilganiga zid. B tajribadan tashqariga chiqadi: so‘lak faqat kesilgan barglarda sinalgan, butun barglarda emas. C mantiqiy tuyulishi mumkin, lekin tadqiqot moddani nima qo‘zg‘atishini o‘lchagan, u qurtlarni qaytarishini emas.

passage: The following text is from an original short story. Mr. Penhallow had promised his niece that the new house would be "modest," and he was a man who kept his promises in letter if not in spirit. The house had only one tower. The ballroom, he liked to point out, was scarcely larger than the one at his club, and the fountain in the front courtyard ran only on Sundays. Whenever guests praised the house, Mr. Penhallow would wave a hand and remind them, with perfect seriousness, that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: he had spared no expense in making it the grandest house in the county.
option_b: he had always preferred a simple way of life.
option_c: his niece had chosen the design of every room herself.
option_d: the house was far too large for a family of his size.
explanation_en:
The narrator mocks Mr. Penhallow for keeping his promise of a "modest" house only "in letter": he treats one tower and a Sunday-only fountain as proof of modesty. In character, he would seriously insist that he prefers a simple life, as in choice B, which is exactly the irony the text builds.

Choice A is true from the reader's point of view, but Mr. Penhallow would never admit it, since he insists the house is modest. Choice C is unsupported; the niece only received the promise. Choice D would be an admission that undercuts his claim of modesty.
explanation_uz:
Hikoyachi Penhallow janoblarini "kamtarona" uy haqidagi va’dasini faqat "so‘zma-so‘z" bajargani uchun masxara qiladi: u bitta minora va faqat yakshanbada ishlaydigan favvorani kamtarlik dalili deb biladi. Uning fe’liga ko‘ra, u jiddiy qiyofada oddiy turmushni afzal ko‘rishini ta’kidlashi kerak — B. Matn aynan shu kinoyani quradi.

A o‘quvchi nuqtai nazaridan to‘g‘ri, lekin Penhallow buni hech qachon tan olmaydi, chunki u uyni kamtarona deb turib oladi. C asossiz: jiyan faqat va’da olgan, xolos. D uning kamtarlik haqidagi da’vosini yo‘qqa chiqaradigan e’tirof bo‘lardi.

passage: A financial company reported that customers who chose to use its budgeting app saved, on average, 30 percent more each month than customers who did not. Economist Kamol Rustamov then studied a group of customers, a randomly selected half of whom were given the app for free while the other half were not. After a year, the customers who had been given the app saved only about 5 percent more each month than the others. Rustamov's results suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: the budgeting app has no effect at all on how much its users save.
option_b: customers in Rustamov's study who received the app saved less than those who did not.
option_c: the company made an arithmetic error when it calculated its 30 percent figure.
option_d: much of the savings gap the company reported probably reflects differences between the customers who chose the app and those who did not, rather than the effect of the app itself.
explanation_en:
When the app was handed out at random, it produced only a 5 percent gain, far less than the 30 percent gap among customers who chose it themselves. The rest of that gap likely comes from the kind of people who choose such an app (for example, people who already care about saving), as choice D says.

Choice A is too extreme: a 5 percent gain is still an effect. Choice B reverses the result. Choice C is unsupported; the company's figure can be calculated correctly and still be misleading about cause.
explanation_uz:
Ilova tasodifiy tarzda berilganda u bor-yo‘g‘i 5 foizlik o‘sish bergan, bu ilovani o‘zi tanlagan mijozlardagi 30 foizlik farqdan ancha kam. Farqning qolgan qismi bunday ilovani tanlaydigan odamlarning o‘ziga xosligidan (masalan, ular tejashga oldindan e’tiborli bo‘lganidan) kelib chiqqan bo‘lishi ehtimoli katta — D.

A haddan oshadi: 5 foizlik o‘sish ham ta’sir hisoblanadi. B natijani teskari aylantiradi. C asossiz: kompaniya raqamni to‘g‘ri hisoblagan bo‘lishi, lekin sabab haqida chalg‘itishi mumkin.

passage: At a fossil site, paleontologist Ilhom Sobirov described 23 trackways left by a small plant-eating dinosaur, all heading northeast. Some researchers argue that the parallel trackways show the animals moved together as a herd. Sobirov cautions, however, that the trackways run along what was once a narrow strip of shoreline between steep cliffs and a lake, and that the mud at the site may have stayed soft enough to record footprints for several weeks. Sobirov's caution suggests that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: the dinosaurs that made the trackways were most likely fleeing from a predator.
option_b: the smaller dinosaurs at the site were following the scent of the larger ones.
option_c: the trackways could have been made by animals walking alone at different times, since the shoreline would have led any animal in the same direction.
option_d: dinosaurs of this kind could not have traveled in herds.
explanation_en:
A narrow shoreline forces any walker in one direction, and soft mud lasting weeks means the tracks need not have been made at the same time. So parallel tracks alone do not prove herding; separate animals could have made them, as choice C says.

Choices A and B offer new explanations that nothing in the text supports. Choice D is too extreme: Sobirov questions whether this site proves herding, not whether herding was possible at all.
explanation_uz:
Tor qirg‘oq har qanday hayvonni bir yo‘nalishda yurishga majbur qiladi, haftalab yumshoq qolgan loy esa izlar bir vaqtda qoldirilmagan bo‘lishi mumkinligini bildiradi. Demak, parallel izlarning o‘zi podani isbotlamaydi, ularni turli vaqtda yolg‘iz yurgan hayvonlar qoldirgan bo‘lishi mumkin — C.

A va B matnda hech qanday asosi bo‘lmagan yangi izohlarni taklif qiladi. D haddan oshadi: Sobirov podada yurish umuman mumkinligini emas, bu joy uni isbotlay olishini shubha ostiga oladi.

passage: A landscape long attributed to the painter Maarten Olde, who died in 1702, was recently found to contain Halden blue, a pigment first manufactured in 1834. Some critics concluded that the painting must be a later imitation. Conservator Aiko Brandt points out, however, that the pigment appears only in a strip of sky along the top edge, an area where X-rays show that damaged paint was scraped away and replaced, and that the rest of the painting contains only pigments that were available before 1700. Brandt's observations suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: the Halden blue may have been added during a later repair, so its presence does not show that the painting as a whole was made after 1834.
option_b: Olde himself must have used Halden blue before it was widely manufactured.
option_c: the painting was certainly made by Olde.
option_d: the damaged strip of sky was repaired before 1702.
explanation_en:
The newer pigment is confined to an area that was scraped and repainted, and the rest uses only early pigments. The pigment therefore points to a later repair, not a later painting, as choice A says.

Choice B conflicts with the dates: Olde died in 1702, long before the pigment existed in 1834. Choice C is too strong; Brandt removes one objection but does not prove who painted it. Choice D is impossible, since the repair contains a pigment first made in 1834.
explanation_uz:
Yangi bo‘yoq faqat qirib tashlanib, qayta bo‘yalgan qismda uchraydi, rasmning qolgan qismida esa faqat eski bo‘yoqlar bor. Demak, bu bo‘yoq rasm keyin chizilganini emas, keyinroq ta’mirlanganini ko‘rsatadi — A.

B sanalarga zid: Olde 1702-yilda vafot etgan, bo‘yoq esa 1834-yilda paydo bo‘lgan. C haddan tashqari qat’iy: Brandt bitta e’tirozni olib tashlaydi, lekin muallifni isbotlamaydi. D bo‘lishi mumkin emas, chunki ta’mirlangan joyda 1834-yilda paydo bo‘lgan bo‘yoq bor.

passage: Corals on Seravin Reef usually bleach, losing the algae that live in their tissues, when the water temperature rises above 31°C. Yet corals of the same species in a shallow lagoon nearby, where summer water often reaches 33°C, rarely bleach. Marine biologist Nilufar Karimova moved fragments of lagoon corals to the reef and fragments of reef corals to the lagoon. Two years later, she exposed all of the fragments to 33°C water in the laboratory. Fragments that had come from the lagoon did not bleach, while fragments that had come from the reef did, regardless of where each fragment had spent the previous two years. These results suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: lagoon water contains a substance that protects corals from heat.
option_b: the lagoon corals' heat tolerance is a lasting trait of those corals rather than a response to the conditions where they currently live.
option_c: reef corals would become heat tolerant if they spent more than two years in the lagoon.
option_d: corals of this species cannot survive in water warmer than 31°C.
explanation_en:
Each fragment's response matched where it came from, not where it had lived for two years. Lagoon corals stayed tolerant even after two years on the cooler reef, so their tolerance is a lasting trait, as choice B says.

Choice A is ruled out because reef corals that lived in lagoon water for two years still bleached. Choice C goes beyond the data; the study lasted only two years and shows no sign of change. Choice D contradicts the lagoon corals, which handled 33°C without bleaching.
explanation_uz:
Har bir bo‘lakning javobi u ikki yil yashagan joyga emas, kelib chiqqan joyiga mos kelgan. Laguna marjonlari ikki yil sovuqroq riflarda yashagandan keyin ham issiqqa chidamli bo‘lib qolgan, demak, bu ularning barqaror xususiyati — B.

A rad etiladi, chunki ikki yil laguna suvida yashagan rif marjonlari baribir oqargan. C ma’lumotlardan tashqariga chiqadi: tadqiqot faqat ikki yil davom etgan va hech qanday o‘zgarish belgisini ko‘rsatmagan. D 33°C da oqarmagan laguna marjonlariga zid.
